explain.es: En el inglés culto, repetir lo que ya se ha dicho suena torpe. Para evitarlo hay dos recursos: la sustitución (cambiar un fragmento por una palabra comodín: so, not, do so, one / ones, that / those, the same) y la elipsis (omitir el fragmento y dejar solo el auxiliar o el to). El español también lo hace, pero con otras piezas («Creo que sí», «Yo también», «Lo intenté»): por eso los calcos delatan incluso a hablantes muy avanzados.
explain.en: Educated English avoids repetition in two ways: substitution (replacing a chunk with a pro-form: so, not, do so, one/ones, that/those, the same) and ellipsis (leaving the chunk out and keeping only the auxiliary or to).

explain.title: 1 · SO y NOT en lugar de una oración
explain.title_en: So and not replacing a clause
explain.es: Tras verbos de opinión y expectativa (think, believe, expect, suppose, imagine, hope, guess, be afraid) y tras seem / appear, una oración completa con that se sustituye por so (afirmativa) o not (negativa): es el equivalente de «que sí», «que no» o «lo». Con think, believe, expect, imagine la negativa natural traslada el no al verbo principal (I don't think so); I think not existe, pero es formal o tajante. Con hope y be afraid solo vale not: I hope not, I'm afraid not (I don't hope so).
explain.en: After verbs of opinion and expectation, a whole that-clause is replaced by so or not. With think/believe/expect/imagine the usual negative is I don't think so; I think not is formal or emphatic. With hope and be afraid only not works.

examples.en: — Will the motion be carried? — I expect so, given the turnout.

explain.title: ¿SO, NOT o nada? Verbo a verbo
head: Verbo
✅ «Que sí»
⛔ «Que no»
rows: I don't think so. (formal: I think not)
I don't know. · I'm not sure. (I know so)
explain.note: La negativa con not detrás (I believe not) es más formal o tajante; la habitual es I don't think / believe so. Con say y tell: If you say so, I told you so; con so delante: So I hear · So it seems (eso he oído / eso parece).
explain.note_en: Verb + not is formal; don't + verb + so is the norm. Also: If you say so · I told you so · So I hear.

explain.title: Truco: la prueba de la reconstrucción
explain.es: Reconstruye mentalmente la frase entera: I'd love to [come] ✓, Yes, I do [like it] ✓. Si al reconstruir sale algo agramatical (I think yes → I think yes the shop is open), el sustituto está mal. Y en cuanto al registro: do so, that of, if so, as did e I believe not son de escritura formal; Me neither, Same here o Might do, de la conversación.
explain.en: Rebuild the full sentence in your head: if it's grammatical, your ellipsis is fine. Do so, that of, if so and as did are formal; me neither, same here and might do are conversational.

explain.title: 2 · DO SO, DO IT, DO THAT y DO
explain.es: Do so sustituye a un verbo de acción con todos sus complementos y es típico del registro formal y escrito (avisos, contratos, ensayos). En la conversación se prefiere do it / do that (acción concreta y deliberada) o, sencillamente, la elipsis con el auxiliar (she did). No funciona con verbos de estado: She knew the answer and I did so too → and so did I. En inglés británico, tras un modal o un auxiliar perfectivo aparece además do solo: — Will you be there? — I may do. · He should have done.
explain.en: Do so replaces an action verb plus its complements; it is formal. Conversation prefers do it / do that or plain ellipsis. Not with stative verbs. British English also uses bare do after modals and perfect auxiliaries: I may do, He should have done.

examples.en: Applicants who wish to withdraw may do so in writing at any time.
examples.es: Los candidatos que deseen retirarse podrán hacerlo por escrito en cualquier momento.

examples.en: The minister was urged to apologise, but declined to do so.

examples.es: — ¿Le has escrito al casero? — Todavía no, pero puede que lo haga luego.

explain.title: 3 · ONE y ONES
explain.es: One (singular) y ones (plural) sustituyen a un sustantivo contable ya mencionado, casi siempre con un modificador delante o detrás: the red one, a cheaper one, the ones on the top shelf, which one?. Restricciones clave: (1) no con incontables (red wine or white, no white one); (2) tras posesivo, mejor el pronombre (mine, Anna's) que my one, muy coloquial; (3) un adjetivo no puede quedarse solo como en español («uno nuevo»): a new → a new one; (4) sin adjetivo, a one → one, y en plural indefinido some / any, no ones.
explain.en: One / ones replace a countable noun, usually with a modifier (the red one, the ones on the left). Not with uncountables, not after possessives in careful style (mine, not my one); an adjective cannot stand alone (a new one); plural indefinite uses some/any.

examples.en: Of all the proposals, the one submitted by the Lisbon team was the most persuasive.
examples.es: De todas las propuestas, la que presentó el equipo de Lisboa fue la más convincente.

examples.en: These figures are more reliable than the ones we published in March.
examples.es: Estas cifras son más fiables que las que publicamos en marzo.

examples.en: — I need a charger. — There's one in the top drawer.
examples.es: — Necesito un cargador. — Hay uno en el cajón de arriba.

explain.title: 4 · Elipsis tras auxiliar, modal y TO
explain.title_en: Ellipsis after auxiliaries, modals and to
explain.es: Cuando el verbo ya se ha dicho, se omite todo lo que va detrás del primer auxiliar o del modal, pero ese auxiliar nunca desaparece: He said he'd help, and he has. Si la frase original no tenía auxiliar, aparece do / does / did. Con el infinitivo ocurre lo mismo: se omite el verbo, pero to se queda (I'd love to), y si el verbo es be o el have perfectivo, se conserva (I hope to be). Tras want o like en subordinadas con if / when / as puede caer incluso el to: Come whenever you like.
explain.en: After an auxiliary or modal, everything that follows can be left out, but the auxiliary stays; if there was none, use do/does/did. After to, the verb disappears but to remains, and be is kept (I hope to be). After like/want in if/when clauses, even to may go.

examples.en: Few expected the coalition to survive the vote, but it did.
examples.es: Pocos esperaban que la coalición sobreviviera a la votación, pero lo hizo.

examples.en: I haven't read the report yet, but I will have by Monday.
examples.es: Aún no he leído el informe, pero lo habré hecho para el lunes.

examples.en: — Would you like to join us for dinner? — I'd love to.
examples.es: — ¿Te apetece cenar con nosotros? — Me encantaría.

examples.en: She isn't fluent in Japanese yet, but she intends to be by next year.
examples.es: Aún no domina el japonés, pero piensa dominarlo el año que viene.

explain.title: 5 · SO, NEITHER y NOR + auxiliar
explain.title_en: Agreeing: so do I, neither can she
explain.es: Para decir «yo también / yo tampoco» con un sujeto nuevo: So (afirmativa) o Neither / Nor (negativa) + auxiliar + sujeto, con inversión. El auxiliar copia el tiempo de la frase anterior. Equivalen a …too y …not either, sin inversión. Ojo al matiz: so + sujeto + auxiliar (sin inversión) no añade a nadie, sino que confirma algo con sorpresa: — You promised to call me! — So I did! (¡Es verdad!). En registro elevado aparece también as + auxiliar + sujeto: She opposed the plan, as did most of the board.
explain.en: So / neither / nor + auxiliary + subject (inverted) add a new subject: So do I, Neither can she. Without inversion, so + subject + auxiliary confirms a fact: So I did! Formal: as did most of the board.

examples.en: The Treasury underestimated the deficit, and so did most independent analysts.
examples.es: Hacienda subestimó el déficit, y también la mayoría de los analistas independientes.

examples.en: I had never heard of the author, and neither had my editor.
examples.es: Yo nunca había oído hablar del autor, y mi editor tampoco.

examples.en: — You've left the lights on again. — So I have. Sorry.
examples.es: — Te has vuelto a dejar las luces encendidas. — Es verdad. Perdona.

explain.title: 6 · Coordinación, comparación y respuestas
explain.title_en: Ellipsis in coordination, comparison and replies
explain.es: En oraciones coordinadas se puede omitir el sujeto o el verbo repetido (gapping), algo muy propio del estilo escrito: Some delegates voted in favour; others, against. En las comparaciones, tras than / as se deja solo el auxiliar: She earns more than I do. En las respuestas basta con la información nueva: — Who wrote it? — Tom did. (no Tom wrote). Y en la conversación se omiten sujeto y auxiliar al comienzo (Sounds good. · Seen Tom?): elipsis situacional, solo para el registro coloquial.
explain.en: Coordination allows the repeated subject or verb to be dropped (gapping: others, against). After than/as, keep the auxiliary: more than I do. Replies give only the new information: Tom did. Casual speech drops an initial subject and auxiliary (Sounds good).

examples.en: The first edition sold well; the second, rather less so.
examples.es: La primera edición se vendió bien; la segunda, bastante menos.

examples.en: The new model consumes far less fuel than the old one did.
examples.es: El nuevo modelo consume mucho menos combustible que el antiguo.

examples.en: — Who authorised the payment? — The finance director did.
examples.es: — ¿Quién autorizó el pago? — El director financiero.

explain.title: 7 · THAT OF, THOSE OF, THE SAME, IF SO
explain.es: En el estilo académico y periodístico, para no repetir un sustantivo seguido de complemento se usa that (of / in) en singular y those (of / in / who / which) en plural: The population of Madrid is larger than that of Barcelona. (the one of Barcelona suena coloquial; than Barcelona compara cosas distintas). Otros comodines formales: the same (I would do the same), likewise, if so / if not (= si es así / si no), more so / less so, so antepuesto en if you so wish.
explain.en: Formal style uses that of / those of to avoid repeating a noun with a complement, plus the same, likewise, if so / if not, more so / less so and if you so wish.
formula: the + nombre + of X … *that / those* + of Y

examples.en: The salaries of junior doctors are lower than those of most civil servants.
examples.es: Los sueldos de los médicos residentes son inferiores a los de la mayoría de los funcionarios.

examples.en: Are the data reliable? If so, the policy must change; if not, we need a new survey.
examples.es: ¿Son fiables los datos? Si es así, hay que cambiar la política; si no, necesitamos una nueva encuesta.

examples.en: Her second novel is ambitious, and her third even more so.
examples.es: Su segunda novela es ambiciosa, y la tercera, todavía más.

explain.title: Coloquial frente a formal
explain.es: La elipsis abunda en la conversación; la sustitución con do so, that of o if so es marca del registro escrito y formal. Elige según el contexto: un informe con Me neither chirría tanto como una charla de bar con Should you wish to do so.
explain.en: Ellipsis dominates conversation; substitutes such as do so, that of and if so mark formal writing.

explain.title: Resumen: ¿qué sustituye qué?
head: Recurso · Device
Sustituye a…
Ejemplo · Example
Español

rows: Espero que sí. · Me temo que no.
He was told to leave and did so.

formal; no con verbos de estado

explain.note: Regla de oro: puedes omitir el verbo, <mark>pero nunca el auxiliar ni el to</mark>.
explain.note_en: Golden rule: drop the verb, never the auxiliary or to.

items.bad: — Is the shop open? — I think yes.
items.why: «Creo que sí» = I think so. Yes no puede sustituir a una oración.
items.why_en: Yes cannot replace a clause: I think so.

items.bad: — Will it rain? — I don't hope so.
items.why: Hope y be afraid niegan con not detrás, nunca con don't.
items.why_en: Hope / be afraid: negative with not.

items.bad: — Is she coming? — I hope it.
items.why: Calco de «eso espero»: una oración se sustituye con so, no con it.
items.why_en: Use so, not it, after hope / think.

items.bad: — Are you certain? — Yes, I'm sure so.
items.why: Know, be sure y be certain no admiten so.
items.why_en: Know and be sure never take so.

items.bad: She doesn't like jazz, but I yes.
items.why: «Yo sí / yo no» exige auxiliar: I do, I can, I have…
items.why_en: 'I yes' doesn't exist: use the auxiliary.

items.bad: — Do you want to come? — Yes, I want.
items.why: Want, like, love, need… no se quedan solos: mantén to o usa el auxiliar.
items.why_en: Keep to, or use the auxiliary.

items.bad: I've lost my umbrella; I'll have to buy a new.
items.why: Calco de «uno nuevo»: el adjetivo no puede ir solo, necesita one.
items.why_en: An adjective can't stand alone: a new one.

items.bad: The climate of Galicia is wetter than Madrid.
items.why: Se compara clima con clima: en registro formal, that of / those of.
items.why_en: Compare like with like: that of / those of.

items.es: ¿Qué quieres evitar repetir? ¿Una oración entera, un verbo con sus complementos o un sustantivo?
items.en: What are you avoiding repeating: a clause, a verb phrase or a noun?

items.es: Oración tras think / hope / expect / be afraid… → so / not. Con know / be sure → nada; con doubt → it.
items.en: Clause after think / hope… → so / not; know, be sure → nothing; doubt → it.

items.es: Verbo → deja el auxiliar (o do / does / did) o el to; en registro formal, do so.
items.en: Verb phrase → keep the auxiliary or to; formal: do so.

items.es: Sustantivo contable → one / ones; con complemento y en registro formal → that / those of; incontable → simple omisión (red wine or white).
items.en: Noun → one / ones; formal with complement → that / those of; uncountable → just omit it.

items.es: ¿Un sujeto nuevo coincide contigo? → so / neither + auxiliar + sujeto.
items.en: New subject agreeing → so / neither + auxiliary + subject.

items.es: Revisa: ¿el auxiliar está en el mismo tiempo? ¿El registro encaja con el texto?
items.en: Check tense agreement and register.

items.q: this year's / are / than / those / of / last year / higher / figures
items.a: This year's figures are higher than those of last year.

items.q: if / so / please / let / us / know
items.a: If so, please let us know.

exercises.title: Elige el registro formal
exercises.es: Estas frases pertenecen a textos formales o académicos. Rodea la opción adecuada.
exercises.en: These sentences come from formal or academic texts. Circle the right option.

items.q: The results of the 2024 survey are more reliable than [those|the ones] of 2020.
items.a: those

items.q: Applicants who have not yet [done so|done it] should register by 30 June.
items.a: done so

items.q: The minister opposed the reform, [as did|like did] the opposition.
items.a: as did

items.q: Is the hypothesis correct? [If so|If yes], further research is needed.
items.a: If so

items.q: — Will the board approve the merger? — I [believe not|reckon not].
items.a: believe not

items.q: Her first study was controversial and her second even [more so|more].
items.a: more so

items.q: Delegates may leave the session early if they [wish so|so wish].
items.a: so wish

items.q: We were asked to submit the report by Monday and duly [did so|made it|did it so].
items.a: did so

items.q: The climate of Galicia differs from [that|this|the one] of Andalusia.
items.a: that

exercises.title: Recupera lo omitido
exercises.es: Escribe completa la parte subrayada, recuperando lo que se ha omitido o sustituido.
exercises.en: Write the underlined part in full, restoring what has been left out or replaced.

items.q: — Are you coming to the party? — I <u>might</u>.
items.a: I might come to the party.

items.q: — Is the bank open today? — <u>I don't think so</u>.
items.a: I don't think (that) the bank is open today.

items.q: She said she'd finish it by Friday, and <u>she did</u>.
items.a: She finished it by Friday.

items.q: I've never been to Peru, but <u>my wife has</u>.
items.a: My wife has been to Peru.

items.q: — Would you like a coffee? — <u>I'd love one</u>.
items.a: I'd love a coffee.

items.q: They asked us to leave the room, and <u>we did so</u>.
items.a: We left the room.

items.q: The rent in London is higher <u>than that in Leeds</u>.
items.a: than the rent in Leeds

items.q: — Has the parcel arrived? — <u>Not yet</u>.
items.a: The parcel hasn't arrived yet.

exercises.title: Caza el error
exercises.es: Cada frase tiene UN error de elipsis o sustitución. Escríbela bien.
exercises.en: Each sentence has ONE ellipsis or substitution mistake. Correct it.

items.q: — Is the café open? — I think yes.
items.a: — Is the café open? — I think so.

items.q: — Will it snow tomorrow? — I don't hope so.
items.a: — Will it snow tomorrow? — I hope not.

items.q: My father can't drive, and neither my mother can.
items.a: My father can't drive, and neither can my mother.

items.q: — Do you enjoy your job? — Yes, I enjoy.
items.a: — Do you enjoy your job? — Yes, I do.

items.q: We were invited to the gala, but we decided not.
items.a: We were invited to the gala, but we decided not to.

items.q: My laptop is very slow, so I'm going to buy a new.
items.a: My laptop is very slow, so I'm going to buy a new one.

items.q: The climate of Seville is hotter than Bilbao.
items.a: The climate of Seville is hotter than that of Bilbao.

items.q: — You've forgotten your keys again! — So I've done!
items.a: — You've forgotten your keys again! — So I have!

items.q: — Has the parcel arrived? — I'm afraid no.
items.a: — Has the parcel arrived? — I'm afraid not.

items.q: If you want to resign, you must do it so in writing.
items.a: If you want to resign, you must do so in writing.

exercises.title: De coloquial a formal
exercises.es: Reescribe cada frase en registro formal usando el recurso indicado entre paréntesis.
exercises.en: Rewrite each sentence in a formal register using the device in brackets.

items.q: If you want to cancel your booking, you can cancel it online.
items.a: If you wish to cancel your booking, you may do so online.

items.q: The CEO backed the merger. Most of the board backed it too.
items.a: The CEO backed the merger, as did most of the board.

items.q: Our results are better than the results of our competitors.
items.a: Our results are better than those of our competitors.

items.q: Is the information correct? If it is, sign below. If it isn't, contact us.
items.a: Is the information correct? If so, please sign below; if not, contact us.

items.q: Portugal's economy grew faster than Spain's economy did.
items.a: The economy of Portugal grew faster than that of Spain.

items.q: — Will the minister resign? — Nah, I don't reckon he will.
items.a: I believe not. / I do not believe so.

items.q: I didn't like the first proposal, and I didn't like the second one either.
items.a: I did not like the first proposal, nor did I like the second.

items.q: She's a really talented painter, and her daughter's even more talented.
items.a: She is a highly talented painter, and her daughter even more so.

exercises.title: Transformaciones con palabra clave
exercises.es: Completa la segunda frase para que signifique lo mismo que la primera. Usa la palabra clave sin cambiarla y entre 2 y 8 palabras (estilo Cambridge C2 Proficiency).
exercises.en: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the key word without changing it, in 2–8 words.

items.q:
Everyone in the department voted against the proposal, and I did too.
→ I voted against the proposal, ________ in the department.
items.a: I voted against the proposal, as did everyone else / and so did everyone else in the department.

items.q:
Participants are free to leave the study at any time if they wish.
→ Participants who wish to leave the study ________ at any time.
items.a: Participants who wish to leave the study may do so / are free to do so at any time.

items.q:
The population of Madrid is far larger than the population of Valencia.
→ Madrid has a population ________ of Valencia.
items.a: Madrid has a population far larger than that / much larger than that of Valencia.

items.q:
If you haven't paid the invoice yet, please pay it immediately.
→ Please pay the invoice immediately if you have ________.
items.a: Please pay the invoice immediately if you have not already done so / not yet done so.

items.q:
If the weather is fine, the ceremony will be held outdoors; otherwise, it will take place in the hall.
→ The ceremony will be held outdoors if the weather is fine; ________ take place in the hall.
items.a: The ceremony will be held outdoors if the weather is fine; if not, it will take place in the hall.

items.q:
She said she would finish her thesis by June, and indeed she finished it by then.
→ She said she would finish her thesis by June, and ________.
items.a: She said she would finish her thesis by June, and so she did / she did so.

items.q:
Salaries in the private sector are higher than salaries in the public sector.
→ Salaries in the public sector are ________ in the private sector.
items.a: Salaries in the public sector are lower than those / not as high as those in the private sector.

items.q:
Neither the minister nor his advisers foresaw the crisis.
→ The minister did not foresee the crisis, ________ his advisers.
items.a: The minister did not foresee the crisis, nor did / and nor did his advisers.

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el artículo. Marca T o F y contesta: ¿a qué se refiere cada sustituto y qué se ha omitido?
exercises.en: Read the article. Tick T or F and answer: what does each substitute refer to, and what has been left out?
exercises.text_title: Should we all work from home?
text: When the pandemic forced millions of employees to work from home, many managers predicted that productivity would collapse. It did not. In fact, several studies suggest that it rose, and those that found a decline attributed it to childcare rather than to remote work itself. Will the trend continue? Most economists believe so, though some are less certain.

Not everyone welcomed the change, however. Younger staff, in particular, missed the office, and so did many of those who lived alone. One recent survey found that their sense of isolation was far greater than that of colleagues with families. Asked whether they would return full time if they could, a third said they would; the rest said they would rather not.

Companies now face a choice. Some have ordered staff back to the office five days a week; others, only two. Those that have done so without consulting their employees have often regretted it. As one manager put it: 'If people are trusted, they deliver. If not, they leave.'

items.q: Productivity fell sharply when people started working from home.
items.why: «It did not» = productivity did not collapse; some studies say it rose.

items.q: Every study found that productivity increased.
items.why: Some studies («those») found a decline.

items.q: Most economists think the trend towards remote work will continue.
items.why: «Most economists believe so» = believe it will continue.

items.q: Many people who lived alone missed the office.
items.why: «…and so did many of those who lived alone».

items.q: What does «those» refer to in paragraph 1?
items.a: The studies that found a decline in productivity.

items.q: In «It did not» (paragraph 1), what has been left out?
items.a: collapse: «Productivity did not collapse.»

items.q: What does «that» replace in «than that of colleagues with families»?
items.a: the sense of isolation (of colleagues with families)

items.q: Write in full: «the rest said they would rather not».
items.a: The rest said they would rather not return (to the office) full time.

items.q: What does «done so» refer to in paragraph 3?
items.a: ordered staff back to the office (on fixed days)

items.q: Write in full: «others, only two».
items.a: Others have ordered staff back to the office for only two days a week.

exercises.title: Traduce al inglés
exercises.es: Traduce sin repetir lo que ya está dicho: usa so / not, one(s), auxiliares, to, do so o that / those.
exercises.en: Translate without repetition: use so / not, one(s), auxiliaries, to, do so or that / those.

items.q: — ¿Vendrá Marta a la cena? — Creo que no.
items.a: — Is Marta coming to the dinner? — I don't think so.

items.q: — ¿Hay algún problema? — Me temo que sí.
items.a: — Is there a problem? — I'm afraid so.

items.q: Nunca he estado en Escocia, y mi mujer tampoco.
items.a: I've never been to Scotland, and neither / nor has my wife.

items.q: No me gustan estos zapatos; prefiero los negros.
items.a: I don't like these shoes; I prefer the black ones.

items.q: — ¿Te apetece venir? — Me encantaría, pero no puedo.
items.a: — Would you like to come? — I'd love to, but I can't.

items.q: La tasa de paro de Andalucía es más alta que la de Aragón.
items.a: The unemployment rate in Andalusia is higher than that in / of Aragon.

items.q: Los socios que deseen votar podrán hacerlo por correo.
items.a: Members who wish to vote may do so by post.

items.q: Si es así, avísenos; si no, no hace falta que haga nada.
items.a: If so, (please) let us know; if not, there is no need to do anything / you needn't do anything.

items.q: Dijo que lo terminaría a tiempo, y así lo hizo.
items.a: She said she would finish it on time, and (so) she did.

items.q: — ¿Has terminado? — Todavía no, pero lo habré hecho para las cinco.
items.a: — Have you finished? — Not yet, but I will have by five.

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Escribe respuestas y textos breves usando elipsis y sustitución. Evita repetir palabras.
exercises.en: Write replies and short texts using ellipsis and substitution. Avoid repetition.

items.q: Responde sin repetir: «Do you think artificial intelligence will replace translators?»
items.a: Ej.: I don't think so, or at least I hope not.

items.q: Escribe un aviso formal (2 frases) para clientes que quieran darse de baja. Usa do so e if so.
items.a: Ej.: Those wishing to cancel may do so online. Already paid? If so, you will be refunded.

items.q: Compara dos ciudades o países usando that of y those of.
items.a: Ej.: Lisbon's climate is milder than that of Oslo; its rents are lower than those of Paris.

items.q: Reacciona a «I've never read Proust» y a «I'd love to live abroad», primero coincidiendo y luego discrepando.
items.a: Ej.: Neither have I. / I have. · So would I. / I wouldn't.

items.q: Escribe un diálogo de 4 líneas con I'm afraid not, I'd love to, one / ones y una respuesta corta con auxiliar.
items.a: Ej.: — Have you booked? — No, we haven't. Any tables free? — I'm afraid not. Would you like to wait at the bar? — I'd love to. Are those stools free? — The ones on the left are.

items.q: Reescribe sin repeticiones: «The government promised to cut taxes, and the government did cut taxes, but the government cut taxes by less than it had promised to cut taxes.»
items.a: Ej.: The government promised to cut taxes, and it did so, but by less than it had promised (to).

items.q: Contesta con una frase elíptica natural: «Have you ever been tempted to give up English?» · «Would you mind reviewing my essay?»
items.a: Ej.: I have, more than once! · Not at all — I'd be happy to.

checklist.es: Digo «creo que sí / espero que no» con so / not, nunca I think yes ni I don't hope so.
checklist.en: I use so / not after think, hope, expect, be afraid…

checklist.es: Uso do so en textos formales y do it / that o el auxiliar en la conversación.
checklist.en: I use do so formally and do it / the auxiliary informally.

checklist.es: Sustituyo nombres contables con one / ones y, en registro formal, con that of / those of.
checklist.en: I replace nouns with one / ones and that of / those of.

checklist.es: Al omitir el verbo mantengo el auxiliar o el to: she didn't, I'd love to.
checklist.en: I keep the auxiliary or to when I drop the verb.

checklist.es: Reacciono con So do I / Neither have I respetando tiempo e inversión, y distingo So I did!
checklist.en: I use so / neither + auxiliary + subject correctly.

checklist.es: Al leer textos complejos, reconstruyo qué recupera cada elipsis o sustituto.
checklist.en: I can track what each ellipsis or substitute refers to.
